unit_name: Exhaust heat recovery on an engine or gas turbine (residual after CHP recovery)
provenance_ref: Recovery unit for source class reject_engine_exhaust (note 23, decided 2026-10-02): an exhaust economiser making hot water from what a CHP's own heat recovery leaves, or from a mechanical-drive engine's whole exhaust. capex: [EPA_CHP_RICE] Table 2-4 (costs in 2013 USD), heat recovery equipment (exhaust economiser, jacket water exchanger, pump, controls) 500 USD/kWe on the 633, 1121 and 3326 kWe systems, against total heat recovered of 815, 1266 and 3126 kW (Table 2-2); per kW of heat 388.3, 442.7 and 532.0 USD, median 442.7, plus labour and materials at 25% = 553.4 USD/kW; / 1.5644 USD per GBP (2013, [ONS_AUSS]) = 353.8 GBP/kW; x 95.1126/82.1933 = 1.15719 (2013 to 2021, COMIT workbook sheet gdp_deflators) = 409.4 GBP/kW; x 31709.8 x 1e-6 = 12.9808 GBPm per PJ/yr (11.39 to 15.60 across the 633 and 3326 kWe systems). CONFIDENCE LOW: it prices the full CHP heat recovery set, an upper anchor for recovering only a residual, which no source prices alone. fixed_opex: GAP; PROXY at the [DECC_SURPLUSHEAT2014_APP] slide 16 worked example's O&M share of capex, 40/600 = 6.67%, so 0.0667 x 12.9808 = 0.86539. lifetime: GAP; PROXY 15 yr, the reciprocating engine plant life of [BEIS_EGC2016] footnote 56. availability_factor: PROXY, chp_gas_turbine's 0.93, since it runs only when its source does. min_viable_scale in PJ/yr of reject_engine_exhaust drawn: the smallest [EPA_CHP_RICE] system (100 kWe, Table 2-2) recovers 0.21 MMBtu/h of exhaust heat = 0.0615 MW x 8760 h x 3600 s = 0.00194 PJ/yr; the smallest catalogued size, not an economic cut-off. grade_out 2: [EPA_CHP_RICE] section 2.4, engine heat recovery makes 190 to 230 F (88 to 110 C) water

unit_name: Water-source heat pump on chiller condenser heat
provenance_ref: Recovery unit for source class reject_chiller_condenser (note 23, decided 2026-10-02): a water-source heat pump lifting chiller condenser heat to about 80 C. [DEA_IPH_2026] datasheet sheet '1.1 Traditional heat pump', heat source 30/20 C excess heat or process cooling, 3 MW unit (range 0.5 to 5 MW), financial data in 2025 euro excluding VAT (catalogue p27). capex: nominal investment 0.95 MEUR/MW (row 19; indirect investment 0.19 MEUR/MW, row 25, excluded) / 1.1673 EUR per GBP (2025, [ONS_THAP]) = 0.81385 GBPm/MW / 1.20887 (2025 to 2021 by [ONS_YBGB], 2024 = 100 vintage, 103.6/85.7; the COMIT gdp_deflators sheet stops at 2022) = 0.67323 x 31.7098 MW per PJ/yr = 21.3479 GBPm per PJ/yr, 2.09 times heat_pump_lt_reject's 10.1966. fixed_opex: fixed O&M 2127 EUR/MW/yr (row 22) converted the same way = 0.04780, plus variable O&M 3.07 EUR/MWh of heat (row 23) = 0.60430 GBPm per PJ of output x availability 0.9808 = 0.59273, folded in because unit.csv has no variable cost column: 0.64053. lifetime: 25 yr technical (row 12, range 15 to 40). availability_factor: heat_pump_lt_reject's 0.9808 (PROXY). min_viable_scale in PJ/yr of reject_chiller_condenser drawn: DEA's lower unit size, 0.5 MW of heat (row 6, note A) x (1 - 1/3.95) = 0.3734 MW x 8760 h x 3600 s = 0.01178 PJ/yr; conservative, since [annex58_t1_2023] lists heat pumps from 30 kW. Coefficients: COP 3.95 (row 31), see unit_input_output.csv
